chapter: Buffalo, Lunceford, Lil Armstrong and Stuff Smith
title: Tommy Stevenson, the high-note man behind "Rhythm Is Our Business"
summary: After Trummy Young joined, Tommy Stevenson came in as the first trumpeter Jones heard hit notes that high; mostly a high-note specialist.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: So he'd played a little. But anyhow, he didn't have too much of that to do, when Trummy come in and tried to put on a third trombone, and they put Trummy in there, you know, Trummy and Wells. And then when I left the band, he brought in Steve, and Steve, that was a great thing. He'd never heard nobody hit no high note like that. Tommy Stevenson?
He's the one who made, "Rhythm is our Business."
That was before Paul come back again.
Yeah. Steve was the first one I ever heard to make notes way up there like that, yeah.
Could he blow good as well?
Mostly high notes. That was his thing, the high note man, you know.
